relevance_note: A review that, besides group counts, gives individual-level detail for a few HA20 patients, e.g. "A patient with ALPS presented with fevers, bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, extensive skin rash, and massive hepatosplenomegaly."
method_note: Review (Aksentijevich & Zhou 2017); most HA20 data are group counts in Table 2 (columns for refs 16, 37, 36, 35). Rows built by a short Python script from my own reading; table spans were taken from the row lines and checked verbatim. In scope: (1) the single patient of ref (35) (Japanese, ALPS; Table 2 column 'Patients (35) (n = 1)'; variant in Figure 2 legend); (2) one patient of Zhou et al. (16) described as initially diagnosed with SLE with CNS vasculitis and ITP; (3) two patients shown in Figure 3D and 3E legends ('a patient with HA20'), recorded as unnamed person 1 and 2 because the paper does not say whether they are the same person or which published patients they are; they could overlap with each other or with the ref (16) patient. Groups from refs (36) and (37) (two Japanese families, n=3 and n=6) have counts only and get no rows. Table 2 column (35) has n = 1: cells '1/1' were recorded as observed for that patient; cells '0/1' were left not reported under the zero-count rule (v4), although with n = 1 they would mean absent; '/' is defined as not reported. Effective treatment for (35) is '0/1; 0/1; 0/1', so treatment is not reported. For the ref (16) patient, Table 2 '11/11' (oral ulcers, early age onset) in the column 'Patients (16) (n = 11)' was recorded as observed, inferred from group statement. Variant for ref (35): the review prints 'the reported p.Gln415fs (35)' and 'reported as c.1245_1248del', and proposes corrected nomenclature c.1249_1252del / p.Lys417Serfs*4; I recorded the originally reported strings (cDNA tie to ref 35 is through the same Figure 2 legend sentence, not explicit). Zygosity, inheritance and variant type left not reported (Table 1 'Heterozygous' is a general disease-level statement). No variant rows for the ref (16) and Figure 3 patients: no variant is printed or tied individually. Possible inconsistency: in Table 2 the 'Elevated CRP, ESR' row reads 6/6 in the n = 11 column and 1/1 in the n = 6 column, which looks shifted; the (35) value 1/1 was still used. 'fevers' mapped to checklist 'recurrent fever'; dermal abscesses mapped to 'skin lesions'. Normal CD3+CD8+ subpopulations recorded as excluded abnormality (D-27).
